record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let M be a complete Riemannian manifold. Does there exist a function f_M, depending on M but invariant under rescaling of the metric, such that every finite connected geodesic net G on M with n unbalanced vertices, total length L, diameter D, and adjusted total length L_tilde has at most f_M(L_tilde, L/D, n) balanced vertices? Here L_tilde is the sum over all arclength-parametrized edges e(s) of the integral of 1/inj_M(e(s)) ds, where inj_M(x) is the injectivity radius at x. In particular, if M has positive injectivity radius inj(M), must every such G have at most f_M(L/inj(M), L/D, n) balanced vertices?

evidence.quote: The adjusted total length L̃ of a geodesic net is the sum of integrals over all edges ei parametrized by their respective arclengths of 1 / inj(ei(s)), where inj(ei(s)) denotes the injectivity radius of the ambient Riemannian manifold at ei(s).

Conjecture 3.4.3 (Boundedness conjecture for geodesic nets on Riemannian manifolds). Let M be a complete Riemannian manifold. There exists a function fM which depends on M but is invariant with respect to rescalings of M with the following property: Let G be a geodesic net on M with total length L, adjusted length L̃ and diameter D that has n unbalanced vertices. Then its number of balanced vertices does not exceed fM (L̃, L / D, n). In particular, if M has injectivity radius inj > 0, then the number of balanced vertices does not exceed fM (L / inj, L / D, n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold. A finite geodesic net on $M$ is a finite connected graph $G$ together with a map from $G$ to $M$ such that each edge is mapped to a geodesic segment (parametrized by arclength). A vertex $v$ of $G$ is called balanced if the sum of the unit tangent vectors at $v$ along the edges incident to $v$ equals zero (as a vector in $T_{\varphi(v)}M$); otherwise it is called unbalanced. Let $L(G)$ denote the total length (sum of edge lengths), $D(G)$ the diameter of $G$ (as a metric space with the induced length metric), and $n(G)$ the number of unbalanced vertices. Let $\mathrm{inj}_M(x)$ denote the injectivity radius of $M$ at $x$, and define the adjusted total length by
$$\widetilde{L}(G) \;=\; \sum_{e} \int_0^{\ell(e)} \frac{ds}{\mathrm{inj}_M(e(s))},$$
where the sum is over all edges $e$ of $G$, parametrized by arclength, and $\ell(e)$ is the length of $e$.

Question: Does there exist a function $f_M:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\times\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\times\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$, depending on $M$ but invariant under rescaling of the Riemannian metric of $M$, such that every finite connected geodesic net $G$ on $M$ satisfies
$$\#\{\text{balanced vertices of }G\} \;\leq\; f_M\!\bigl(\widetilde{L}(G),\;L(G)/D(G),\;n(G)\bigr)?$$

In particular, if $M$ has positive global injectivity radius $\mathrm{inj}(M)>0$, must every such $G$ satisfy
$$\#\{\text{balanced vertices of }G\} \;\leq\; f_M\!\bigl(L(G)/\mathrm{inj}(M),\;L(G)/D(G),\;n(G)\bigr)?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The boundedness question for balanced vertices of geodesic nets in terms of unbalanced (boundary) vertices and metric data is a well-known open problem originating with Gromov. Recent work (e.g., 2024–2025 preprints) addresses specific subcases: a single balanced vertex in nets with three boundary vertices in non-positively curved planes, and constructions suggesting unboundedness in the four-boundary-vertex case. The general conjecture for complete Riemannian manifolds with the adjusted-length and L/D parameters does not appear to be resolved.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work aims to construct geodesic nets with four boundary vertices and arbitrarily many balanced vertices, suggesting unboundedness in that regime.
status_evidence.claim: The general boundedness question remains open; subcases are being investigated.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of a balanced vertex in geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Each geodesic net with three unbalanced vertices on a non-positively curved Riemannian plane has at most one balanced vertex.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results in low boundary-vertex cases are known.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists boundedness conjectures for geodesic nets as open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is listed as an open problem.
